editorial:
After losing her grandmother, eight-year-old Nelly wanders into the woods and meets a girl who looks and acts just like her. Their instant friendship feels warm and strange at the same time, and the movie turns a quiet family story into a gentle fantasy about grief, memory, and the bond between mothers and daughters. You feel the sadness, but also a soft sense of wonder as Nelly learns more about her mom through this mysterious new friend.

The acting is natural and deeply moving, especially from the young leads, and the slow, calm pacing lets every small moment land. It is short, sweet, and emotionally rich, though some viewers may want more action or a bigger twist. If you enjoy thoughtful family dramas with a magical touch, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Nelly realizes the girl she has been playing with is her mother, Marion, as a child. Their time together helps Nelly understand why her mom is hurting after Grandma’s death. Before saying goodbye, young Marion goes to the hospital for an operation, and Nelly returns to her own time. Back home, adult Marion comes back, and mother and daughter share a quiet, healing moment together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet family stories with a magical touch.
